title: Terminal-Register Certification for Finite-Measurement Learning of Multiscale Quantum States
abstract: Learns 1D pure states with an inverse binary MERA whose coarse-grained-away qubits are measured together at a terminal register; finite-shot certificate with a noise-aware implementation budget. On an open-boundary TFIM ground state, a frozen 8-qubit schedule reaches mean fidelity 0.996886 (60/60 held-out runs > 0.99). At n=16, MERA beats a causal-cone-complete, parameter-matched local circuit in all 30 paired comparisons (fidelity, long-range error, energy, entropy) despite the local circuit's 2.62x gate exposure; no run met the stationarity criterion.
key_claims: Inverse-MERA learning with terminal measurement reproduces the sequential bit-string distribution
Parameter-matched causal-cone-complete local circuit loses 30/30 to MERA at n=16 (unconverged)
relevance_note: Abstract only. Binary (not ternary) MERA on TFIM at 8-16 qubits with a matched local-circuit control, the control design RESEARCH-DIRECTOR section 19 asks for. Possible protocol reference for a hardware MERA-prep leg (Helios path); touches no anchor. The MERA-vs-local advantage comes from unconverged optimizations, so it is weak evidence.
